Inorganic_Organic_Ratio_SEI_CEI.source_text: Compared to CCE, the weaker Crelated signals in both DEE electrolytes suggested suppressed decomposition of the organic solvents Fig. S38a. The higher concentration of LiDFOB in the 1.2 m MSN-LD promoted the formation of a B/F-rich anion-derived CEI layer Fig. 6i and Fig. S38b to enhance both the ionic conductivity and mechanical stability. Meanwhile, the signals detected from the N 1 s and S 2p spectra indicated that SN and MSM also participated in CEI formation, which contained mathrm 3 mathrm N , , to further enhance ion transport Fig. 6j, l. The O 1 s spectra Fig. 6k revealed that the CEI formed in the CCE contained mathrm x y O z a typical reaction product of mathrm 6 with carbonate solvent, which generated HF to corrode the electrodes and accelerate the capacity decay 53. In contrast, the CEIs formed in the DEE electrolytes were entirely devoid of mathrm x y O z , exhibiting higher chemical stability. Notably, the absence of the mathrm - O peak from the 1.2 m MSN-LD spectrum confirmed the existence of a dense, homogeneous CEI layer that effectively passivated the cathode surface, suppressing Co dissolution and mitigating structural degradation 54.
